evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'Find the env var set on your laptop and nowhere else.' plus one line ('a command-line checker... scans your codebase for every variable it reads, compares that list with .env.example and your CI config, and exits non-zero when one is missing or unused') and the action '$ npx envcensus' / 'Copy the scan command'. As the developer who once shipped a deploy that broke on a missing variable, the headline names my exact incident; I could repeat what it does after one read.
evidence.fit: Both audiences get a path: the hero is aimed at the individual developer ('on your laptop'), and the CI section says outright 'This is the step for the team that owns CI' with a workflow step, job log, exit codes and a 'Copy the workflow step' button. Brief constraints reflected: npm only, 'no Homebrew formula yet' (Reference > Install), 'repository is private until 1.0' (Source note and footer), help output presented as the documentation, no GUI screenshots, no stars or users claimed. The no-benchmark fact is respected by silence rather than addressed.
evidence.distinctiveness: Monospace headline and a three-pane trace (src/config.ts, .env.example, ci.yml) that highlights where the selected variable is read and set. That trace is drawn from the product's own model (three lists compared) rather than a template. The overall structure is still a fairly familiar hero, explainer table, CI and reference layout.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the 'What a run prints, on a sample repo' report sits in the first viewport, labelled 'Example output' at the top. Clicking each of the 5 rows updates an explanation below the table and highlights the line in each source pane: FEATURE_FLAGS_URL shows 'missing here' in .env.example and 'not set here' in ci.yml. There are small internal inconsistencies. The summary reads '3 problems: 1 missing, 2 not set, 1 unused' (four findings), and the job log lists four lines under '3 problems'. The CI step runs 'npx envcensus --ci' with no argument, but the help defines '--ci <file>'.
evidence.craft: The type scale and spacing are clean and consistent, rows are 44px buttons, and the selected-row highlight is clear. A defect: at 1440 the '$ envcensus --help' block is cut off inside its 670px box (scrollWidth 829), so the defaults column is clipped on desktop and needs a sideways scroll in the box (axe scrollable-region-focusable). Nav wraps to a second row at 390 and 320 but stays tidy.
evidence.mobile: 390: the report is recomposed from table columns into stacked per-variable cards (code / .env.example / ci.yml), so nothing overflows (overflow 0 at 390 and 320). The copy button is 48px tall, and tapping it shows 'Copied: npx envcensus' directly under the buttons. Nav links are 44px tall. Drawback: the artifact starts below the first screen at 390, and after tapping an upper row the explanation (top 1071) and source panes appear below the visible rows.
evidence.honesty: Each example is labelled where it appears. The report says 'Example output. The column layout of the shipped build may differ'. The CI block says 'Example step; adapt to your CI', and the job log says 'Example output on the sample repo above'. The help says 'Example of the help text; run the command for the shipped version' and 'Flag names can change before 1.0; the shipped text wins'. The primary action says exactly what it does: 'Copy the scan command' copied 'npx envcensus' in my test. 'Runs on your machine and sends nothing anywhere' matches the brief.
evidence.interaction: 1440 and 390 (tap): all 5 report rows respond, setting aria-pressed and updating the detail text and the state label in each pane. 'Copy the scan command' (hero and footer) and 'Copy the workflow step' write to the clipboard, verified as 'npx envcensus' and the two-line workflow step, with inline status text. There is a fallback message if the clipboard is unreachable. Keyboard: skip link first, focus outline (2px solid) on every stop, Enter on a row selects it. No console errors at any width.
evidence.copy: Specific and from the developer's world: 'A new teammate copies the example and the app breaks on first run', 'turns "works on my machine" into a check that runs on every push, with no service to host and no agent to install', 'If your variables live only in a secrets manager... envcensus has nothing to compare and is not for you yet.' Button labels say what happens. Slight repetition: the privacy line appears twice nearly verbatim.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, the action and a labelled, operable sample report are all in one viewport, which earns full marks. 390: the promise, the command box and 'Copy the scan command' are visible, but the sample report is below the fold, so nothing in view backs up the promise on a phone.

problems: The sample's counts don't add up: '3 problems: 1 missing, 2 not set, 1 unused' (and four log lines under '3 problems'), and the CI step uses '--ci' with no file while the help says '--ci <file>'. A skeptical developer notices this in the example meant to build trust.
At 1440 the --help block is clipped inside its box and needs a sideways scroll, on the page section that is supposed to be the documentation.
On a phone the artifact is below the first screen, and row-tap feedback lands below the rows.

evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'Every environment variable your code reads, checked against .env.example and CI.' with a supporting paragraph ('lists each variable with the line that reads it, and tells you which ones nobody set and which ones nothing reads anymore') and '$ npx envcensus' + Copy. What it does is very clear. Who it is for is implied (anyone with code and a .env.example) and not named. The headline describes a mechanism, not a pain.
evidence.fit: Covers the brief closely. The CI section opens 'If you own the pipeline rather than the application: it is one step, needs no token, and makes no outbound request', and it defines what 'set in CI' means, a real platform-engineer question. The 'Where it stands' list addresses each brief fact (on npm, source private until 1.0, no Homebrew, no speed numbers, no users) in a confident voice. The help output is framed as the documentation. The two audiences are handled through sections rather than a hero that names either one.
evidence.distinctiveness: Serif body with a terminal 'ledger' table as the hero artifact and dark code panes. It is restrained and editorial, with no template cards or logo strips. Distinctive mainly through tone and the table, with a conventional section sequence.
evidence.proof: A 12-row census table ('~/code/orders-api $ envcensus', 'scanned 212 files in 3 directories') starts at y=588 on 1440, so it is partly in the first viewport. Its counts are consistent (11 read, 3 missing, 1 unused, exit 1), and the GitHub annotation log matches the workflow shown. It is static, and it is identified only by a caption below the table ('A run against a small Node service'), never called an example or sample. At 390 the 'read at' file:line column is hidden, which drops the detail the headline promises.
evidence.craft: Calm hierarchy and generous spacing. The serif stack (Charter fallback) renders as a generic Times-like serif on this machine, which reads less deliberate. The load-time row fade (70ms stagger) leaves the table blank in early or full-page captures. At 390 the nav links are 25px tall. No overlap or clipping at 1440, 768 or 390.
evidence.mobile: 390: overflow 0. The table reflows to variable / .env.example / ci.yml, with the verdict tucked under the variable name, which stays readable. The copy button is 57px tall, and the 'Copied npx envcensus' toast appears at the bottom-centre after tapping. Nav targets are only 25px tall. The 'read at' column is removed. The table header only just enters the first screen. Code panes scroll sideways inside their boxes (541-567px wide in 351px).
evidence.honesty: 'Where it stands' handles caution well: 'speed: No published numbers... this page will not quote a figure it cannot back', 'users: None to name'. Copy says what it copies. However, the sample run is presented as a real run of a named repo, with no 'example' label next to it. The --help block is presented as authoritative ('This is what envcensus --help prints... If a flag is not listed below, it does not exist'), and 'what counts as a read' asserts Python, Go, Ruby and shell support. None of this is in the brief, and none of it is hedged. As the founder, I would be putting specific flags and language support on record under my name.
evidence.interaction: The only control is the Copy button. At 1440 and 390 (tap) it copied 'npx envcensus' and showed a 'Copied npx envcensus' toast. Keyboard focus is visible (2px outline) on nav, Copy and the footer link. The brand link goes to '#'. The census table, the page's artifact, does not respond to anything, so a visitor cannot query it. No console errors.
evidence.copy: The best writing of the two. 'gets a stack trace instead of a login page', 'the real failure waits for production', 'every new hire sets it anyway, and nobody is sure what is safe to remove', 'If it finds something in your code, that is the testimonial.' Terms are consistent and every sentence carries information. The bare 'Copy' label works because it sits beside the command.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: promise, command and Copy, plus the top six rows of the census table are in view, but the table's label (a caption below the table) is not. 390: promise and command plus Copy are in view, and only the table header line peeks in at the bottom. The promise is specific and believable but only half-backed in view.

problems: The help text and language support ('what counts as a read') are asserted as fact with 'If a flag is not listed below, it does not exist', though the brief supplies neither. The sample run is never labelled as an example where it appears.
The artifact is static. The page's only interaction is one Copy button, so a visitor cannot explore the finding they care about.
Mobile details: nav targets are 25px, the 'read at' column is dropped at 390, and the artifact sits mostly below the first screen.

reason: As the developer, A names my exact incident in the headline and lets me click a variable to trace it through code, .env.example and ci.yml in the first screen. As the founder, A labels every example and hedges the help text, so it doesn't commit me to flags or language support I haven't confirmed. B has the better prose and the more candid 'Where it stands' section. Two things would change my mind: if B's help text and language list are confirmed accurate, or if A's sample counts ('3 problems' for four findings) and the '--ci' mismatch are judged worse than B's unlabelled run.
